_note: Where the lawn's light actually comes from, and what colour it is when it arrives. A mown lawn seen low is a mirror of the sky at a shallow angle, and the mint veil is that mirror: `sheen` (specularIntensity) is the share of the pixel the sky owns and `albedoColor` is the share the grass owns. These cases trade one against the other at the SAME brightness, and add a warm bias to the grass's share, so the mint can be traded for grass without the garden going dark. Picks are fractions of the frame, on places read off `pictures/2112-southborder.png` and friends: a place given in metres has to be found before it is believed.
